Hi Arielle — thanks for the note. Looping in Laura (Security) and Aditya (Legal ops) to confirm process and owners. Quick answers up front, then we can schedule a short call if you want to walk through examples.

- Notification owner: Security incidents are initially routed to security@redwood.com. Primary on-call: laura.bennett@redwood.com. Backup: sergio.alvarez@redwood.com.
- Evidence handback: our standard is to preserve full forensic artifacts for 90 days post-incident; upon formal evidence request we aim to hand over relevant logs within 48 business hours for severity-high incidents. Larger requests or export of raw packet captures may take up to 7 business days.
- Escalation queue: if PoC doesn't respond within 24 hours (for severity-high), the next rung is Security Director (laura.bennett), then Legal (aditya_rao), then CTO/direct leadership for executive notifications.

I attached a proposed timeline spreadsheet with suggested windows based on severity categories. Laura — can you confirm any operational constraints or required redaction steps before we provide artifacts?

Best,
Sergio

Thanks — the summary from Sergio is correct. A couple operational notes:

- Preservation: we snapshot affected instance logs and key-value cache artifacts immediately and replicate to a secured retention bucket. That snapshot persists at least 90 days; extended retention possible via support agreement.
- Evidence delivery format: CSV/NDJSON logs for application-level events, pcap/PCAPNG only under strict NDA for customers who require network captures — we redact internal customer IDs by default.
- SLA nuance: 48 business hours for targeted log exports (severity-high). For legal eDiscovery requests we coordinate with Aditya and may need 3–5 business days for legal review.

Arielle — to set expectations for procurement, for severity-high incidents we commit to initial acknowledgement within 2 hours, triage summary within 8 hours, and evidence handback within 48 business hours (subject to legal holds). For severity-medium: acknowledgement within 8 business hours and evidence within 5 business days.

I'll attach the evidence packaging guidance we send to external partners.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Hi all — quick clarifications from Legal:

- SLA clock: evidence SLA begins when Redwood confirms the scope of the request in writing to the requester. If redaction is required and scope is disputed, the clock pauses until scope is agreed (we'll log timestamps for audit). We will, however, provide a triage summary within the original 48-hour window even if redaction scope is pending.
- Evidence transfer sign-off: legal sign-off is required on the transfer form for any PII-sensitive artifacts; otherwise Security may sign for purely operational logs. I'll attach a short template clause you can drop into the SOW.

Action items:
1) Sergio — please confirm the exact PoC emails and backup names for the SOW.
2) Laura — please confirm whether GreenFin's standard evidence checklist (Arielle) requires network captures; if so we need an NDA addendum.
3) Morgan — once PoC names are in the SOW we can insert the SLA language and re-submit.

Aditya Rao
